headline: Engineering doors opened through jobs, projects, training and promotion
summary: Black engineers designed infrastructure, changed aircraft production, led space projects and taught the next generation. These records separate earning a degree from getting hired, being assigned technical work and gaining authority to lead.
coverageNote: Nine selected episodes across civil, mechanical, aerospace and systems engineering. Named employers include Michigan Central Railroad, Tennessee State, NASA Langley, Boeing, The Aerospace Corporation and NASA Goddard. Their records do not establish every engineering specialty or a reader’s own employment chain.
question: Which hiring, project assignment, qualification or promotion record connects Black engineers to your workplace?

events.title: William Hunter Dammond takes a winding route into railroad engineering
events.decisionMaker: Michigan Central Railroad employed him; the account does not name the hiring official.
events.barrier: A civil-engineering degree did not lead directly to an engineering job.
events.change: After graduating from Pitt in 1893, Dammond held other jobs and taught mathematics before becoming an assistant bridge engineer in Detroit.
events.outcome: Railway-signal patents followed in 1903 and 1906; recognition for his inventions remained contested.
events.limit: The biography does not date the railroad hire or establish continuity to a present-day railroad employer.

source.title: University of Pittsburgh · William Hunter Dammond
source.supports: Degree, intervening jobs, Michigan Central employment and patents.

events.title: Howard's trustees authorize engineering degree programs
events.people: Howard's trustees, faculty and engineering students
events.decisionMaker: Howard University's Board of Trustees approved the programs in 1907.
events.barrier: The college identifies educating Black engineers as its institutional mission; this source does not describe each student's admissions barriers.
events.change: Civil, electrical and mechanical engineering entered the curriculum over the following years.
events.outcome: By 1911 Howard had established a four-year bachelor's curriculum and an equipped school building.
events.limit: Program creation establishes education, not an employer's hiring practices or every graduate's placement.

source.title: Howard University College of Engineering and Architecture · Our History
source.locator: 1907 trustees' approval; 1907–1910 curriculum and 1911 four-year program paragraphs
source.supports: Trustee approval, discipline-specific curricula and the four-year degree program.

events.title: Archibald Alexander enters civil engineering and starts a firm
events.decisionMaker: Marsh Engineering hired Alexander; he later established his own company.
events.barrier: Iowa identifies him as its first Black civil-engineering graduate.
events.change: After graduating in 1912, he joined Marsh and founded a company in 1914.
events.outcome: His later firm’s projects included Iowa’s power plant and Moton Airfield.
events.limit: These are individual employment and project records, not evidence of industry-wide access.

source.title: University of Iowa College of Engineering · Archibald A. Alexander
source.locator: Biography: graduation, Marsh employment and later projects
source.supports: Degree, engineering employment and firm ownership.

events.title: Yvonne Young Clark teaches engineers and leads a department
events.decisionMaker: Tennessee Agricultural & Industrial State University, now Tennessee State, hired her as an instructor.
events.barrier: TSU identifies Clark as the first woman on its engineering faculty.
events.change: Her 1956 appointment put a Black woman in a paid engineering teaching role.
events.outcome: She advanced to associate professor, twice chaired mechanical engineering and retired in 2011 after decades of mentoring students.
events.limit: Faculty employment and mentorship are documented; this source does not measure graduates’ hiring outcomes.

source.title: Tennessee State University · Remembering Yvonne Young Clark
source.locator: 2019 remembrance: appointment, department leadership and retirement
source.supports: 1956 instructor hire, later rank and leadership, and student recollections.

events.title: Mary Jackson trains and earns promotion at Langley
events.people: Mary W. Jackson and Kazimierz Czarnecki
events.decisionMaker: Hampton permitted her attendance; Langley promoted her after training.
events.barrier: Required graduate classes met at segregated Hampton High School.
events.change: Encouraged by Czarnecki, Jackson obtained permission and completed the classes.
events.outcome: NASA records her 1958 engineering promotion and supersonic-aerodynamics research.
events.limit: This establishes advancement at Langley, not equal promotion opportunities across NASA or other employers.

source.title: NASA · Mary W. Jackson
source.supports: Training access, Langley promotion and subsequent engineering work.

events.title: Walt Braithwaite helps change how Boeing designs aircraft
events.decisionMaker: Boeing hired Braithwaite as a tool engineer in 1966.
events.barrier: Entry into engineering, control of technical projects and corporate leadership were separate career stages.
events.change: He later introduced networked design and manufacturing systems while supervising Central Engineering.
events.outcome: The museum’s interview-based biography documents technical leadership before his later presidency of Boeing Africa.
events.limit: The record identifies Boeing, not a particular factory or a policy that guaranteed other Black engineers promotion.

source.title: The Museum of Flight · Walt W. Braithwaite
source.locator: Biographical note: hiring, Central Engineering and Boeing Africa
source.type: Archive biography based on participant interview
source.supports: 1966 engineering hire and subsequent design-system and leadership responsibilities.

events.title: Black engineering students turn local support into a national organization
events.people: Edward Barnette Jr., Fred Cooper, Arthur Bond and Purdue's Chicago Six
events.decisionMaker: Student organizers and their faculty adviser formed the local group; participating students established NSBE nationally.
events.barrier: The organizers addressed Black engineering students' recruitment, retention and professional representation.
events.change: The Purdue group invited students from other campuses to build a national organization.
events.outcome: NSBE reports that 134 students from 28 schools gathered at Purdue on April 10–12, 1975.
events.limit: The meeting and organization are documented; the source does not isolate their effect on a particular student's graduation or job.

source.title: National Society of Black Engineers · Convention media kit
source.supports: Purdue student organizing and the dated national founding meeting.

events.title: Wanda Austin moves from engineering work into organization leadership
events.decisionMaker: The Aerospace Corporation employed Austin from 1979 and appointed her president and CEO in 2008.
events.barrier: A technical job and authority to direct engineering teams require different appointments.
events.change: Her roles included leading military-satellite communications and the Engineering and Technology Group.
events.outcome: USC records her as the company’s first Black and first woman president.
events.limit: Her advancement is documented; these biographies do not establish company-wide promotion rates or a route into a reader’s team.

source.title: USC Industrial and Systems Engineering · Wanda Austin
source.supports: 1979 employment, technical leadership roles and 2008 appointment.

sources.title: USC Board of Trustees · Wanda Austin
sources.supports: The explicitly scoped Black and woman leadership milestones at Aerospace.

events.title: Aprille Ericsson builds a career on Goddard spacecraft instruments
events.decisionMaker: NASA Goddard employed Ericsson as an engineer in 1992; the newsletter does not name the hiring official.
events.barrier: Engineering employment, instrument assignments and project management are different steps.
events.change: NASA’s dated account follows her from engineering entry through work on several space missions.
events.outcome: It credits contributions to Webb, the Advanced Topographic Laser Altimeter System and the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.
events.limit: This is Goddard employment and project evidence through 2022, not proof of her current role or a connection to every NASA center.

source.title: NASA Goddard · Innovation Catalyst, June 2022
source.locator: Printed page 4: Celebrating a Goddard African American Innovator; indexed text reviewed
source.supports: 1992 engineer hire and named mission contributions.

sources.title: NASA Goddard · Aprille Joy Ericsson lecture biography
sources.locator: Speaker biography: instrument project manager and technologist
sources.supports: Corroborates Goddard instrument-engineering and project-management work; not current employment status.

furtherResearch: Find dated hiring, project-credit and promotion records for the reader’s exact facility and engineering specialty; a parent organization alone may be insufficient.
Research professional licensure and supervised practice separately where the particular discipline requires them.
Read Braithwaite’s interview and contemporary Boeing project records to identify when design systems were adopted, by whom and at which sites.
Trace historical company names, reorganizations and facilities before connecting Dammond or Alexander to a modern employer.
Expand chemical, industrial, electrical and environmental engineering with their own employment evidence; the examples here do not substitute for those histories.
